title: He didn’t think anyone would see it.
paragraphs: He didn’t think anyone would see it.

Not the first time.
Not the quiet shift in his heart.
Not the moment authority stopped feeling like stewardship… and started feeling like ownership.
And that’s where it always begins.

“He’s delayed.”
“I still have time.”
“No one will know.”
Jesus said it plainly in Matthew 24:48–49—the servant “says in his heart, ‘My master is delayed,’ and begins to beat his fellow servants and eat and drink with drunkards.”
He said it in his heart first.

Before the actions… there was a whisper.
Before the fall… there was permission.
And if we’re honest—this is where it hits.

Because misuse of authority doesn’t always look like abuse on the outside.
Sometimes it looks like control hidden behind “care.”
Pride dressed as leadership.
Silence where there should’ve been courage.
Correction without compassion.

Have you ever used your position… to protect your ego instead of people?
Have you ever delayed obedience because you assumed grace would wait?

That quiet compromise?
That “I’ll fix it later”?
That hidden arrogance no one sees?
And here’s the part we don’t preach enough:

The servant didn’t just hurt others.
He forgot the Master was coming back.

When eternity fades,
accountability fades with it.

When Jesus feels distant,
sin feels small.
Luke 12:45–46 echoes the same warning—when the servant thinks the master is gone, he lives differently… but the master returns “at an hour he does not expect.”
Delayed judgment is not canceled judgment.
That’s the illusion killing souls quietly.

You’re still gifted.
Still positioned.
Still trusted.

Prayer became optional.
Conviction became negotiable.
And influence started feeding identity instead of surrendering to Christ.
This is the part no one says out loud:

Some people don’t lose authority…
they corrupt it slowly.

Smiling in public.
Drifting in private.
Proverbs 16:18 says, “Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.” Not after. Before.
Which means if pride is growing… something is already breaking.
You don’t misuse authority overnight—you drift from intimacy with God first.
If Jesus returned today—would your private life agree with your public calling?

Because this isn’t about “leaders out there.”
This is about every space God entrusted to you.

Your home.
Your words.
Your hidden habits.
Your influence—even if it’s just one person watching your life.
Romans 14:12 reminds us, “Each of us will give an account of himself to God.”

Not your pastor.
Not your parents.
You.
Because some of you reading this aren’t just convicted—

You know exactly where you’ve crossed lines.
Where you’ve justified tone, attitude, silence, control, pride.
You didn’t mean to go this far.
And now shame is whispering, “You’ve already ruined it.”
That’s not the voice of Jesus.
Because the story doesn’t end with a servant who failed.
It points to a Servant who never did.

Philippians 2:6–8 says though He was in the form of God, He “did not count equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied Himself… becoming obedient to the point of death—even death on a cross.”
He chose to be crushed for them.

That includes your misuse.
Your pride.
Your silent compromise.
At the cross, the judgment you deserve… met the mercy you didn’t earn.
Not that you fix yourself to be worthy.
But that you repent—and Christ restores you.
1 John 1:9 promises, “If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us… and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”

Grace is not permission to continue.
Grace is power to change.
If your version of grace allows you to keep sinning comfortably—you’re not following Jesus, you’re avoiding Him.
Because real grace confronts… then transforms.

You are not a ruler of what God gave you.
You are a steward under the authority of Christ.

Name it clearly.
Bring it into the light.
Turn from it—not halfway, not emotionally—fully.

If you’ve wounded someone, go make it right.
If pride has grown, humble yourself before God.
James 4:6 says, “God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.”
For those who are done playing church and ready to walk with Jesus in truth.
There’s another word coming that will confront what you’ve been avoiding.
Check the comments too—there’s something waiting there for you.
